quantities: n_e, T_e profiles; electron distribution constraints
method: For calibrated profiles, compute profile summaries and gradients. For calibrated raw spectra, fit a non-relativistic Gaussian Doppler profile with linear background and Gaussian instrument-width deconvolution to estimate electron temperature. User-defined spectral models can be registered in Python for experiment-specific fitting without modifying the built-in model.
caveat: Raw-spectrum fitting is scoped to non-collective, non-relativistic Maxwellian scattering and a Gaussian instrument response. Density is never inferred from uncalibrated spectral amplitude; calibrated profile, calibrated single-band power-density, and combined spectrum-to-temperature/density workflows are separate explicit modes. A generic custom-model registry supports user-provided fitting functions, but physical interpretation and validation remain the model author's responsibility.
implementation_status: Complete within the explicitly supported computational scope; experimental calibration and independent device-specific validation remain the user's responsibility.

assumptions: Inputs are calibrated radial profiles, not raw detector counts or uncalibrated spectra.
Radius is a one-dimensional unique coordinate in metres; samples are sorted internally.
Volume averages use circular, large-aspect-ratio weighting proportional to minor radius and are not equilibrium reconstruction.
preprocessing: Validate finite values, matching lengths, unique radii, non-negative density/temperature and optional uncertainties; sort all profile channels consistently.
execution_contract.algorithm: Two explicitly separated paths: calibrated profile summaries/gradients; and raw-spectrum Gaussian Doppler fitting with instrumental-width deconvolution to estimate electron temperature. The separate single-band scattered-power helper estimates density only when optical power and geometry are calibrated. A combined calibrated-spectrum entry point now orchestrates spectral fitting and the calibrated-power density relation.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Raw-spectrum temperature uncertainty is local covariance-based and excludes uncertainty in laser wavelength, scattering angle, and instrumental width. Optional independent uncertainties for calibrated scattered-power density are propagated to first order. Profile pointwise uncertainties are propagated through finite-difference gradients, normalized gradients, local scale lengths, and line/approximate volume averages assuming independent samples; peak-location uncertainty is not estimated.
limitations: Power-based density helper requires calibrated collected power, laser power, interaction length, scattering geometry, collection solid angle and optical efficiency.
Single-band power relation neglects spectral-response integration, stray-light subtraction and relativistic spectral-shape effects.
Numerical gradients can amplify measurement noise; use appropriate smoothing only with a justified noise model.
Raw-spectrum fit uses a Gaussian non-relativistic Maxwellian approximation and requires a known Gaussian instrumental width.
Raw-spectrum fit does not infer density from fitted amplitude; absolute density requires a separately calibrated power/throughput model.
Scattered-power density uncertainty propagation assumes independent input uncertainties and excludes covariance and model/calibration discrepancy.
Profile uncertainty propagation assumes independent pointwise errors and excludes covariance, calibration uncertainty, and model discrepancy.
execution_contract.note: The supported built-in profile, raw-spectrum temperature-fit, calibrated-power density, and combined spectrum-to-temperature/density workflows have dashboard entry points and focused tests. The user-defined spectral-model extension is a Python API, not a dashboard workflow. Overall status remains conservative because independent experimental validation and broader physics models are not claimed. The custom-model registry is process-local and shared by code in the same Python process; it is not per-user isolation for multi-user web deployments.

This status does not claim collective/relativistic inversion, arbitrary non-Maxwellian reconstruction, or independent experimental validation.

quantities: I–V curve, T_e, V_f, V_p estimate, density/flux estimates
method: Analyze a calibrated single-probe I–V sweep with explicit current polarity and user-selected electron-retarding and ion-branch fit intervals. Report floating-potential zero crossing, dI/dV plasma-potential proxy, optional log-linear electron-temperature fit, ion-branch fit and optional sheath-model ion-density estimate when geometry and ion mass are supplied.
caveat: This is a single-probe, model-dependent workflow, not an automatic substitute for calibration or device-specific sheath theory. Fit windows must be physically justified; estimates are sensitive to magnetic field, collisions, RF pickup, secondary emission, sheath expansion, sweep direction and surface condition.
implementation_status: Implemented single-sweep I–V analysis with explicit current convention, descriptive saturation-tail fallbacks, optional fit-window-based Te and ion-branch estimates, and optional model-dependent density inference. Independent experimental validation and full uncertainty propagation are not claimed.

assumptions: Voltage and current are calibrated and synchronized samples from a quasi-static single-probe I–V sweep.
The electron-retarding branch is adequately described by an exponential current after subtracting the ion-current baseline.
The ion branch and collection model are appropriate for the experimental regime; the user selects fit intervals and geometry.
Ion density uses n_i≈|I_isat|/(sheath_factor·e·A·c_s), with c_s=sqrt(e·(gamma_i·T_i+T_e)/(m_i)); all temperatures are in eV.
preprocessing: Require matching one-dimensional voltage/current arrays and at least eight valid distinct voltage points.
Discard non-finite pairs; sort voltage-current pairs together; average currents at duplicate voltages.
Validate current polarity, fit windows, and positive finite geometry/model inputs; fit windows must have two finite strictly increasing bounds.
Use explicit analyst-selected fit windows; no automatic physical regime selection.
execution_contract.algorithm: Validate and clean a one-dimensional calibrated I–V sweep; sort paired samples and average duplicate voltages; calculate every floating-potential zero crossing (including zero-plateau midpoint handling and explicit ambiguity), dI/dV plasma-potential proxy and descriptive saturation-tail currents; optionally fit an ion branch and a log-linear electron-retarding branch; optionally infer ion density only with valid fit, geometry and ion-mass inputs.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Only the optional electron-temperature fit returns a local regression standard error when enough fit points are available. Calibration, current/voltage covariance, fit-window sensitivity, sheath-model uncertainty and density uncertainty are not propagated.
limitations: Saturation-tail estimates are descriptive fallbacks and are not substitutes for a physically selected ion-saturation interval.
Plasma-potential output is a dI/dV proxy, not a universally valid Vp measurement.
Density is a model-dependent estimate; calibration and full uncertainty propagation are not automatic.
Check fit quality and probe-specific sheath, magnetic-field, RF, collision, surface and sweep-direction effects.
execution_contract.note: Complete only within this declared calibrated single-sweep I–V model scope. Fit-window validation and zero-crossing ambiguity are explicit. The software does not calibrate the instrument or automatically choose physically valid fit intervals; independent device-specific validation remains necessary.

quantities: ECE resonance mapping, calibrated brightness/electron-temperature estimate, channel fluctuations and spectra
method: Validated ECE workflow: non-relativistic harmonic resonance field; optional simplified circular-toroidal-field resonance mapping; calibrated spectral-radiance to Rayleigh–Jeans brightness temperature; multichannel fluctuation RMS and one-sided FFT PSD with sampling/Nyquist metadata.
caveat: Brightness temperature approximates electron temperature only for optically thick, thermalized emission. Accurate channel-to-flux-surface mapping requires equilibrium reconstruction and ray tracing; account for relativistic/Doppler shifts, harmonics, polarization/mode, optical depth, calibration, bandwidth, IF response, and nonthermal populations. Simplified circular B(R) mapping is explicitly approximate.
implementation_status: Implemented numerical workflow with explicit calibration/equilibrium limitations; experimental calibration and device-specific validation remain required.

assumptions: Channel frequencies are calibrated and strictly increasing.
Resonance formula assumes non-relativistic electrons and specified harmonic.
Rayleigh–Jeans brightness temperature requires calibrated spectral radiance.
Temperature interpretation requires optically thick, thermalized emission.
FFT mode requires finite, approximately uniformly sampled channels.
preprocessing: Verify frequency/time units and calibration provenance.
Check channel ordering, bandwidth, saturation, missing samples, and noise floor.
For fluctuations, subtract per-channel mean and report Nyquist frequency.
execution_contract.algorithm: Compute f_ce=s*e*B/(2*pi*m_e); optionally invert B(R)=B_axis*R_axis/R. For calibrated radiance compute T_b=c^2 I_nu/(2 k_B f^2), then express k_B*T_b in eV. For fluctuation mode compute per-channel RMS and one-sided FFT PSD.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: No universal uncertainty is inferred. Propagate supplied calibration, radiance, frequency, bandwidth, equilibrium, and noise uncertainties externally; outputs are deterministic conditional on inputs.
limitations: No raw receiver/IF calibration or instrument response deconvolution.
No automatic EFIT equilibrium, ray tracing, polarization, relativistic/Doppler correction, or optical-depth solver.
Circular-field radius is a simplified estimate, not a flux-surface coordinate.
Brightness temperature is not automatically electron temperature.
FFT PSD is a basic periodogram, not Welch-averaged or confidence-bounded.
execution_contract.note: Implemented callable analysis pipeline; do not imply instrument calibration or equilibrium-grade localization.

quantities: T_i, toroidal/poloidal rotation, impurity density constraints
method: Fit a calibrated isolated charge-exchange emission line with a Gaussian plus local linear background; subtract a known Gaussian instrumental width in quadrature to estimate ion temperature and Doppler line-of-sight velocity.
caveat: Requires correct line identification, calibrated wavelength axis, rest wavelength, emitting-ion mass, and independently measured instrumental sigma (not FWHM). This workflow does not perform atomic-rate impurity-density estimation, neutral-beam attenuation, or toroidal/poloidal inversion.
implementation_status: Complete within the explicitly supported calibrated single-line analysis scope; multi-view inversion, impurity density, atomic kinetics and device-specific validation are explicitly out of scope.

assumptions: Wavelength axis is calibrated and strictly increasing.
Line is isolated, optically thin, and correctly identified.
Emitting-ion velocity distribution is a single Maxwellian.
Doppler and instrumental profiles are Gaussian.
Rest wavelength, ion mass, and instrumental standard deviation are known.
preprocessing: Validate dimensions, finite values, monotonic wavelength, positive physical parameters and optional uncertainties.
Estimate a local linear edge background and fit Gaussian amplitude, center, width, intercept and slope.
Reject unresolved line widths when observed width does not exceed instrumental width.
execution_contract.algorithm: Fit Gaussian emission plus local linear background using nonlinear least squares. Compute intrinsic Doppler sigma from sqrt(sigma_observed^2 - sigma_instrument^2), Ti = m_i c^2/e * (sigma_D/lambda_0)^2, and v_los = c*(lambda_center-lambda_0)/lambda_0. Propagate local fit covariance to Ti and line-of-sight velocity uncertainties. The declared completion boundary is calibrated isolated-line inference only; no uncalibrated detector-to-physics claim is made.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: Local nonlinear least-squares covariance; optional per-sample standard deviations enable weighted fitting. Ti and velocity uncertainties are first-order covariance propagation. Excludes systematic uncertainty and covariance in wavelength calibration, rest wavelength, ion mass, and instrumental width.
limitations: No atomic-rate or neutral-beam attenuation model and no impurity-density estimate.
No toroidal/poloidal rotation inversion; reported velocity is line-of-sight only.
No line deblending, opacity correction, non-Maxwellian distribution, or non-Gaussian instrumental response.
Viewing angle is metadata only and does not perform geometric deprojection.
Covariance-based errors omit calibration and model systematics; independent experimental validation remains required.
execution_contract.note: Complete for calibrated isolated-line fitting and its documented outputs. Not a full CXRS diagnostic suite: impurity density, atomic-rate modelling, neutral-beam attenuation, line deblending, multi-view toroidal/poloidal inversion, and independent device-specific validation are outside scope.

output_specs.description: Explicit model and uncertainty assumptions.

assumptions: Wavelength axis is calibrated and the rest transition and ion species are correctly identified.
The feature is an isolated Gaussian emission line over a locally linear background.
Instrumental and thermal Doppler profiles are Gaussian and independent, permitting quadrature width subtraction.
Nonthermal flow distributions and Stark, Zeeman, opacity, unresolved blend/fine-structure broadening are negligible or separately corrected.
preprocessing: Reject nonfinite, mismatched, non-1D, too-short, or non-increasing wavelength arrays.
Require positive rest wavelength and ion mass; the rest wavelength must fall within the measured wavelength window.
Validate finite nonnegative instrumental width and positive finite per-sample intensity uncertainties when supplied.
Reject flat/no-contrast spectra and emission peaks at the spectral-window boundary.
Fit a Gaussian amplitude and center with positive sigma plus linear local background; convert fit failures and nonphysical fit parameters into clear validation errors.
Reject fitted centers at the wavelength-window boundary, excessively broad fits, and unresolved widths when observed FWHM does not exceed instrumental FWHM.
execution_contract.algorithm: Fit an isolated line to a Gaussian with linear background. Reject out-of-window rest wavelengths, boundary-truncated peaks/centers, failed/nonphysical fits and line widths too broad for the selected window. Convert fitted sigma to observed FWHM, deconvolve known Gaussian instrumental FWHM in quadrature, then calculate Ti using Ti[eV] = (mi c^2/e) (FWHM_D/lambda0)^2/(8 ln 2). Return fitted spectrum, residuals, fit covariance, R-squared and assumptions.
execution_contract.uncertainty_model: When intensity uncertainties are supplied, use weighted nonlinear least squares with absolute sigma. Otherwise use the fitter's residual-scaled covariance. Propagate observed-width and instrumental-width uncertainty to Ti by first-order independent-error propagation when both are available. Excludes wavelength calibration, ion-mass, instrument-model and physical-model discrepancy.
limitations: Not a general Voigt, Stark/Zeeman, opacity, unresolved multiplet or non-Maxwellian line-shape solver.
Fit quality metrics do not prove that the fitted width is thermal.
Instrument width must correspond to the same wavelength, spectrometer configuration, slit/grating and optical path.
Near the instrumental-resolution limit, Ti and its uncertainty become poorly identifiable; unresolved widths are rejected.
Temperature uncertainty excludes systematic wavelength calibration, rest-wavelength, mass, calibration and model uncertainties.
execution_contract.note: Complete only within the explicitly scoped Gaussian isolated-line workflow; experimental physical review remains required.
